Bitcoin.notes: Authorizes spends with ECDSA over secp256k1 (Schnorr/Taproot added 2021, but ECDSA dominates legacy UTXOs) - every legacy signature's safety rests on nonce quality.

CRQC.notes: Cryptographically relevant quantum computer: enough logical qubits + error correction to run Shor against RSA-2048/ECC at operational cost. No public evidence one exists today. Resource estimates have compressed (20M -> <1M -> possibly ~100k physical, contested).

SHIP_Packaging.notes: State-of-the-art Heterogeneous Integrated Packaging. DoD access to advanced 2.5D/3D packaging + chiplets - the other half of trusted assurance beyond the fab.

NIST.notes: US standards body for FIPS crypto. Runs the PQC competition and Dual_EC history.

Thales.notes: SafeNet Luna HSM with FIPS 203/204/205. MultiApp 5.2 Premium PQC smart card (Oct 2025 Europe).

Caltech.notes: Robert McEliece (Caltech/JPL) proposed the code-based McEliece cryptosystem (1978) - ~47 years unbroken, a leading conservative PQC candidate.

Brown_University.notes: Hoffstein, Pipher, Silverman built NTRU (1996) - the first practical lattice-based public-key scheme and a direct ancestor of today's lattice PQC.

TU_Darmstadt.notes: Buchmann/Dahmen/Huelsing built XMSS (eXtended Merkle Signature Scheme) - stateful hash-based signatures, the most conservative PQC signatures (RFC 8391).

Tel_Aviv_University.notes: Oded Regev (TAU/NYU) introduced Learning With Errors (LWE, 2005) - the hardness assumption underpinning the NIST lattice standards.

Max_Planck.notes: Max Planck Institute for Security & Privacy (Peter Schwabe) co-authored CRYSTALS-Kyber/Dilithium (ML-KEM/ML-DSA). With Radboud + Ru Bochum, the European academic core of PQC standardization.

University_of_Waterloo.notes: Institute for Quantum Computing + Centre for Applied Cryptographic Research (Menezes et al.; ECC/PQC). A historic crypto powerhouse whose co-op pipeline feeds Big Tech; with Perimeter Institute anchors Canada's quantum sector.

McEliece_Cryptosystem.notes: Code-based crypto - a main PQC family (Classic McEliece; HQC), the conservative non-lattice branch. Long keys but decades of cryptanalysis behind it.

NTRU.notes: First practical lattice cryptosystem. IP passed NTRU Cryptosystems -> Security Innovation -> OnBoard Security -> Qualcomm (2019). NIST PQC round-3 finalist and conceptual precursor to ML-KEM/ML-DSA.

XMSS.notes: Hash-based stateful signatures (RFC 8391). With LMS, the hash-only-assumption branch that became SLH-DSA (FIPS 205). Deployed by the Quantum Resistant Ledger.

LWE.notes: Learning With Errors / Module-LWE - the mathematical basis of ML-KEM (Kyber) and ML-DSA (Dilithium), the primary NIST PQC standards.

ML_KEM.notes: NIST FIPS 203 (CRYSTALS-Kyber) lattice KEM. Primary PQC encryption primitive.

Lattice.notes: Anduril command-and-control / sensor-fusion software. NATO E-ACCS reporting (2026) pairs Lattice with Palantir in alliance C2 awards.

SLH_DSA.notes: NIST FIPS 205 (SPHINCS+) hash-based signatures. Conservative PQC backup.

OFAC.notes: Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control. Runs the SDN sanctions list; its Tornado Cash designation was the first against autonomous smart-contract code - and the first to be judicially vacated.

FinCEN.notes: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. Money-transmitter registration/AML regime under which mixer operators are charged.

Financial_Privacy.notes: The legitimate demand the mixers also serve: on-chain pseudonymity is not anonymity, and public ledgers expose everyone's balances/history. The privacy case that makes mixers dual-use rather than purely criminal.

AES_256.notes: Symmetric block cipher. Grover gives quadratic speedup only; 256-bit remains the post-quantum symmetric baseline.

Dual_EC_DRBG.notes: NIST SP 800-90 Dual_EC_DRBG. Public controversy over NSA-influenced constants; withdrawn. Historical dual-use of a standard.

IETF.notes: TLS, IPsec, and protocol crypto. Hybrid TLS (X25519MLKEM768) work in progress.

NSA_CNSA2.notes: NSA Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0: mandates PQC transition for NSS.

Whitfield_Diffie.notes: Public-key exchange; later public critic of key-escrow.

Daniel_J_Bernstein.notes: NaCl/libsodium, Ed25519, SPHINCS; public Dual_EC critic.

Peter_Shor.notes: Shor's algorithm: polynomial-time factoring and discrete log on a quantum computer.

Microsoft.notes: OS, identity, mail, EDR (Defender), cloud. Recurring target AND default protector. Dual-use node.

ECDSA.notes: Elliptic Curve DSA over secp256k1/P-256. Signature security collapses if the per-signature nonce k is reused (same r -> solve for private key d, closed-form) or biased/partially known (lattice attack on the Hidden Number Problem).

Weak_Nonce_Failure.notes: In the wild: Brengel & Rossow parsed 647M BTC signatures, found 1,068 reused r-values across 4,433 keys; the 2013 Android SecureRandom bug reused k and drained wallets; Biased Nonce Sense (2019) and 'Chain Reactions' (2026, Polygon MEV) recovered ETH/BTC keys.

ECDSA_fail_Tracker.notes: The 'ECDSA.fail' premise: a living scanner/disclosure thread continuously cataloging chains and libraries for repeated/biased/related nonces and surfacing affected signatures. Local analogue: the ecdsafail-cli skill.

RFC6979_Deterministic.notes: Derives k deterministically as HMAC(message-hash, secret-key) - same message always yields the same k, removing RNG dependence and eliminating the reuse/bias vector for correct implementations.

EdDSA_Ed25519.notes: Derives the nonce deterministically from private key + message by design, structurally preventing RNG-driven reuse; increasingly preferred for new systems. Does NOT address the quantum break.

QRL.notes: The Quantum Resistant Ledger uses stateful hash-based signatures (XMSS) instead of ECDSA - positioned explicitly as post-ECDSA/post-quantum.

Ethereum.notes: EOAs sign with ECDSA/secp256k1; the same nonce-quality dependence applies chain-wide.

Paras_Jha.notes: Co-author of the Mirai IoT botnet; pleaded guilty (2017). Originally built to attack Minecraft DDoS-protection markets before it escaped control.

Hector_Monsegur.notes: 'Sabu' - leader/hub of LulzSec (and AntiSec). After his 2011 arrest he became an FBI informant; his cooperation led to arrests of fellow members. The canonical flip of a hacktivist leader to dismantle a leaderless crew from within.

Mirai.notes: 2016 IoT botnet: enslaved insecure devices via default creds into a massive DDoS engine. Hit Krebs-on-Security, OVH, and via Dyn (Oct 21 2016) knocked out Twitter/Netflix/Reddit across the US East Coast. Source code was released publicly, spawning countless variants.

ILOVEYOU_Worm.notes: May 2000 email worm ('LOVE-LETTER-FOR-YOU.txt.vbs'). Overwrote files, mailed itself to the whole Outlook address book; ~$5-10B in damage. The law-lags-tech precedent: author never charged.

WannaCry.notes: 2017 worm ransomware on EternalBlue. Lazarus public attribution (UK/US).

Worm.notes: Self-replicating (WannaCry/EternalBlue, Conficker). Recurring target = unpatched SMB/RDP.

Stuxnet.notes: The first known cyber-physical weapon (~2010). Targeted Siemens S7 PLCs driving Natanz enrichment centrifuges, subtly varying rotor speed while replaying normal readings to operators. Used 4 zero-days + stolen code-signing certs; spread via USB across air gaps. Widely attributed to a US-Israel operation ('Olympic Games'); never officially claimed.

Natanz.notes: Iran's uranium-enrichment facility. Physical target of Stuxnet - the demonstration that code can destroy hardware and set back a national program without a kinetic strike.

BlackEnergy3.notes: Sandworm's tool in the Dec 2015 Ukraine grid attack - the first confirmed cyber-caused blackout (~230k people). Operators watched their own cursors open breakers; KillDisk wiped systems and firmware bricked serial-to-ethernet converters to slow recovery.

Industroyer.notes: aka CRASHOVERRIDE. Sandworm's Dec 2016 Kyiv attack - the first malware purpose-built to speak grid protocols (IEC 60870-5-101/104, IEC 61850, OPC DA) and trip breakers autonomously, no operator needed. A reusable grid-attack framework, not a one-off.

Industroyer2.notes: 2022 Sandworm variant deployed against a Ukrainian energy provider during the war; hard-coded to specific substation configs. Blunted by defenders (ESET/CERT-UA) - the grid-attack lineage continuing under wartime conditions.

Triton_TRISIS.notes: aka HatMan. 2017 attack on a Saudi petrochemical plant targeting Schneider Triconex Safety Instrumented Systems - the emergency shutdown layer. The first malware built to disable the safety system protecting human life; a plant trip (not detonation) exposed it. Attributed to Russia's TsNIIKhM (XENOTIME).

PIPEDREAM.notes: aka INCONTROLLER (2022). A modular OT-attack toolkit (CHERNOVITE) able to target Schneider/Omron PLCs and CODESYS/Modbus/OPC-UA generically - the first cross-industry, reusable ICS malware framework, discovered before deployment.

XENOTIME.notes: The Triton actor (linked to Russia's TsNIIKhM). Notable for expanding reconnaissance to US/other electric utilities after the Saudi SIS attack - the group willing to touch safety systems.

Safety_Instrumented_System.notes: SIS: the independent last-line controllers that trip a process to a safe state (emergency shutdown). Attacking the SIS removes the barrier between a cyber incident and physical harm - the line Triton crossed.

OT_Protocols.notes: Modbus, DNP3, IEC 60870/61850, S7comm, OPC, CODESYS - the industrial protocols, mostly designed pre-internet with no authentication. The trust assumption ICS malware weaponizes.

Water_Utility_SCADA.notes: Municipal water/wastewater SCADA - under-resourced, often internet-exposed HMIs with shared/default creds. Oldsmar FL (2021) lye-dose tampering and 2023-24 Unitronics PLC defacements (pro-Iran) show the low bar to reach human-safety systems.

SACLA.notes: SPring-8 Angstrom Compact Free Electron Laser. Harima Science Garden City (Sayo, Hyogo), Japan. SLAC.notes: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory. Operates LCLS.

HQC.notes: NIST selected HQC (Mar 2025) as code-based backup KEM.

EDR_XDR.notes: Endpoint telemetry + behavioral detection. Works vs known malware and many living-off-land patterns. Fails vs BYOVD/EDR-killers, signed-driver abuse, and when the EDR process itself is injectable.

Network_Segmentation.notes: Blast-radius limit. Works vs worm/ransomware east-west spread. Fails when identity IS the network (token/TGT replay across segments).

Immutable_Backups.notes: Recovery from encryption. Works if backup plane is identity-isolated. Fails if AD/backup-admin is taken first (Conti playbook).

Memory_Safe_Rewrites.notes: Removes a class of bugs (CISA/NSA memory-safety guidance). Works vs memory-corruption worms. Fails vs logic/authz/supply-chain.

Allowlisting_PPL.notes: Application control + Protected Process Light for security services. The documented mitigation for DoubleAgent-class verifier-DLL injection into AV.

Vulnerable_Driver_Blocklist.notes: Microsoft HVCI/WDAC blocklist vs BYOVD. Coverage lags newly-abused signed drivers (AuKill, EDRKillShifter).

SIEM_Detection_Engineering.notes: Log correlation. Works when telemetry exists and detections are tuned. Fails if EDR is killed first or logs are not collected from appliances.

PQC_Migration.notes: Hybrid TLS + ML-KEM/ML-DSA. Works for NEW sessions after cutover. Does not un-harvest old ciphertext (HNDL already incurred).

DoubleAgent.notes: 2017 Cybellum: Application Verifier DLL injection into AV processes. Requires prior admin. Mitigation = PPL.

Active_Directory.notes: Windows identity plane. Kerberos/NTLM/Golden Ticket. Recurring because it IS the network.

Huntress.notes: Managed security platform for SMBs and MSPs: owned Managed EDR + Managed ITDR (Microsoft 365 identities) + Managed SIEM + SAT, operated by a 24/7 human-led SOC. CVE Numbering Authority. Distinct from CrowdStrike-class enterprise EDR sold as a console; Huntress sells the SOC as the product. Vendor-claimed scale (endpoints/identities) is not independently audited here.

Huntress_SOC.notes: 24/7 SOC wrapping Huntress telemetry. Why it works for SMBs: detection-to-remediation is staffed, so a shop without a SOC still gets a human on the incident. Failure mode is the same as any EDR-backed SOC: if the agent is killed (BYOVD/EDR-killer) or identity is reset via helpdesk, the SOC sees a hole, not a guarantee.

Managed_ITDR.notes: Identity threat detection and response on Microsoft 365. Adjacent to helpdesk-vishing (Scattered Spider): it can see anomalous identity use after the fact; it does not replace phishing-resistant MFA or a helpdesk that will not reset on a phone call.

MSP_Channel.notes: Outsourced IT / MSP channel. Huntress's primary distribution is through MSPs protecting many small tenants, not Fortune-500 SOC buy. That is a different concentration: one MSP compromise or one bad tenant config fans out.

Snyk.notes: Developer security platform: Snyk Open Source (SCA), Snyk Code (SAST), Snyk Container, Snyk IaC, plus secrets and (2026) agentic/AI-code validation. Sits in the IDE/CLI/PR, not in the SOC. Distinct from Huntress (MDR) and CrowdStrike (endpoint EDR). Founded on open-source vulnerability intel; Trust Center lists ISO 27001 / SOC2. Customer-code-not-used-for-training is a vendor policy claim.

SCA.notes: Software composition analysis: known vulns and licenses in third-party packages. Why it works: most app risk is transitive deps, not first-party logic, and SCA is the control that sees the SBOM. Failure: 0-days not yet in the intel DB; unreachable CVEs as noise; does not stop a malicious maintainer who ships a clean version then a bad one (xz-utils / npm worm class) until the signature is published.

FinSpy.notes: Gamma's modular implant (calls, messages, mic/camera, files). Amnesty (Sep 2020) found new variants targeting Egyptian civil society and first publicly revealed FinSpy for macOS and Linux alongside Windows/Android.

Hacking_Team.notes: Milan; 'Remote Control System' / Galileo, sold to abusive governments. Itself hacked in 2015 (400GB dump) confirming client lists incl. Sudan/Ethiopia. Wound down / reformed as Memento Labs.

Candiru.notes: Tel Aviv (aka Sourgum). 'DevilsTongue' Windows spyware used against civil society across multiple countries. Added to US Commerce Entity List (2021) alongside NSO.

Hack_For_Hire.notes: The mercenary phishing/hack-for-hire market. 'Dark Basin' (Citizen Lab, 2020) tied an operation targeting thousands (climate advocates, journalists) to India-based BellTroX - distinct from implant vendors but same clientele.

Shai_Hulud.notes: First wave detected 2025-09-16: ~187 npm packages compromised (incl. several tied to CrowdStrike). Self-replicating: steals npm token, injects an install hook into the victim's other packages, republishes an incremented patch, repeats. Harvests secrets with TruffleHog and exfiltrates to attacker-created PUBLIC GitHub repos; registers victims as self-hosted GitHub Actions runners for persistence.

Shai_Hulud_V2.notes: 'Sha1-Hulud: The Second Coming'. Second wave 2025-11-21..24: 700+ packages, 27,000+ malicious repos, ~14,000 secrets across 487 orgs (ranges vary by vendor). Escalation: runs during PRE-install (not post-install), uses the Bun runtime, and carries a DESTRUCTIVE dead-man payload (wipes home directory if it cannot exfiltrate).

Mini_Shai_Hulud.notes: 4th-generation variant, active since late Apr-2026, most destructive in the 2026-05-11 wave; actor self-labeled 'TeamPCP'. New tricks: PROVENANCE-ATTESTATION FORGERY and AI-CODING-AGENT persistence - deliberately targeting the AI-developer supply chain (tools with elevated filesystem access).

GitHub.notes: Microsoft-owned. In this campaign it is simultaneously the exfiltration surface (attacker-created public repos), the propagation surface (Actions runners), and the host of the compromised CI/CD.

ctrl_tinycolor.notes: @ctrl/tinycolor - a widely-depended-on npm color utility, among the patient-zero packages of the first wave. Illustrates blast radius: one small transitive dependency reaches thousands of downstream builds.

CICD_Pipeline.notes: GitHub Actions / CI runners. Both a victim (secrets in env, build access) and the propagation surface: the worm registers victim machines as self-hosted runners for persistence and re-execution.

Cloud_Credentials.notes: npm/GitHub PATs and AWS/GCP/Azure keys harvested from developer machines and CI env. ~14,000 secrets exfiltrated in the V2 wave; dumped to public GitHub repos for anyone to reuse.

Npm_Maintainer_Account.notes: The registry publisher account. Initial access to the first wave is attributed to phishing that harvested maintainer npm tokens (fake 'npmjs support' / lookalike domains). One stolen token = publish rights across all that maintainer's packages.

AI_Coding_Agent.notes: AI dev tools/agents with elevated filesystem + token access. Mini Shai-Hulud specifically targets this tier - trust + automation concentrated in a component that reads secrets and writes code.

NPM_Lifecycle_Hooks.notes: VECTOR: npm's pre/post-install lifecycle scripts run arbitrary code at `npm install` time. The worm injects an install hook into every package it can publish - the mechanism of both infection and self-replication. V2 moved to PRE-install to fire earlier.

Maintainer_Phishing.notes: VECTOR (initial access): credential-phishing of package maintainers via lookalike registry domains to steal npm publish tokens - the human foothold that seeds the automated spread.

TruffleHog_Weaponized.notes: VECTOR (collection): the worm bundles TruffleHog - a legitimate secret-scanning tool - to sweep the victim host/repo for tokens and cloud keys. Dual-use: the same scanner defenders run to find leaked secrets.

CICD_Runner_Persistence.notes: VECTOR (persistence): registers the victim as a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner, giving the attacker durable code execution inside the CI environment that survives the initial package removal.

Provenance_Forgery.notes: VECTOR (defense evasion): Mini forges npm provenance/attestation metadata so a poisoned package appears to have a trustworthy build origin - defeating the exact control introduced to stop supply-chain tampering.

Disable_Install_Scripts.notes: MITIGATION: install with lifecycle scripts disabled (`npm ci --ignore-scripts`, or `ignore-scripts=true`) so a poisoned package cannot execute on install. Directly neutralizes the primary infection mechanism.

Trusted_Publishing_OIDC.notes: MITIGATION: publish via short-lived OIDC 'trusted publishing' + granular/expiring tokens instead of long-lived PATs; enforce 2FA/passkeys on registry accounts. Removes the reusable-token loot the worm needs to republish.

Dependency_Pinning_Cooldown.notes: MITIGATION: pin exact versions via lockfile + integrity hashes and quarantine brand-new releases for a cooldown window - so a malicious patch bump is not pulled the moment it is published.

NPM_Provenance_Attestation.notes: MITIGATION (partially defeated): sigstore-backed npm provenance ties a package to its source + build. Strong against blind tampering - but Mini's forgery shows attestation is only as good as the trust in the signing path.

Ephemeral_CI_LeastPriv.notes: MITIGATION: ephemeral, isolated CI runners with least-privilege scoped secrets and egress filtering - so a compromised build cannot persist as a runner, read every secret, or phone home to GitHub-hosted drops.

Secret_Rotation_Scanning.notes: MITIGATION (response): continuous secret scanning + fast rotation. Because dumped secrets are public immediately, detection-to-rotation time is the whole game post-compromise.

Canvas/Instructure, Carnival, Charter, Rockstar, Telus, the European Commission. Leaks/sells via BreachForums-lineage and direct extortion.

Florida_DMV.notes: State of Florida DMV / FLHSMV. CLAIMED by ShinyHunters on a leak site (published 2026-09-07; 'FINAL WARNING', deadline 2026-09-11; no ransom figure stated). Data claimed: driver-license info, photos, signatures, addresses, vehicle records from Florida's DAVID system. UNVERIFIED and credibility-questioned: the published 'proof' was an EXPIRED record tied to Jeffrey Epstein that had already appeared in public DOJ documents - so it does not establish current DAVID access. FLHSMV issued no confirmation. No acquisition vector disclosed.

Snowflake.notes: Cloud data-warehouse whose customer tenants were mass-raided in 2024 via stolen credentials against accounts lacking MFA - the incident that scaled ShinyHunters into hundreds of millions of records. The platform was not breached; customer credential hygiene was.

Salesforce.notes: SaaS CRM at the center of the 2025-26 campaign: ShinyHunters abused OAuth-connected apps (Salesloft/Drift-style integrations) and Experience Cloud misconfigurations to pull customer data from many downstream tenants at once.

Voice_Phishing.notes: VECTOR (initial access): AI-assisted vishing (Vapi, Bland AI) impersonating IT/helpdesk to harvest SSO credentials and push MFA enrollment - the human-first foothold shared with Scattered Spider / The Com.

OAuth_Token_Abuse.notes: VECTOR (supply chain): stealing/abusing OAuth tokens from connected third-party SaaS apps to reach the primary tenant's data without a password or MFA prompt - one integration compromise fans out to hundreds of victims.

Data_Extortion.notes: The business model: exfiltrate and threaten publication for payment - no encryption. Lower operational cost than ransomware and sidesteps backup-based recovery entirely; leverage is reputational + regulatory, not availability.

OAuth_Scope_Minimization.notes: MITIGATION: inventory connected OAuth apps, minimize granted scopes, short-lived tokens, and revoke/rotate on anomaly - shrinks the blast radius of a compromised integration.

Cylance.notes: AI endpoint security (pre-CrowdStrike-era ML antivirus). In-Q-Tel-backed; acquired by BlackBerry (2018, ~$1.4B).

HawkEye_360.notes: Smallsat constellations geolocating RF emissions (ships going dark, jamming, comms) - space-based signals intelligence as a service. In-Q-Tel-backed; sells RF-geolocation to NGA/defense/IC.

Fivecast.notes: OSINT / social-media risk analytics used by IC + law enforcement. In-Q-Tel-backed (Australian-origin, Five Eyes).

NGA.notes: National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. Buyer of commercial geoint/RF (HawkEye 360, Planet-type imagery) - the tasking hub wiring commercial-space SIGINT-adjacent data into the IC.

BlackBerry.notes: Pivoted from handsets to security software; owns Cylance endpoint AI and QNX embedded OS.

SIGINT_Collection.notes: Signals intelligence - RF/comms interception and geolocation. Historically a state monopoly (NSA/GCHQ); HawkEye 360-class commercial constellations now sell RF-geoint as a service, blurring the state/commercial line.

OSINT_Collection.notes: Open-source / social-media intelligence (SOCMINT): harvesting and analytics over public data. Sold commercially (Fivecast) to IC + law enforcement - lower legal bar than SIGINT, expanding fast.

DMEA_TAPO.notes: Defense Microelectronics Activity / Trusted Access Program Office. Administers Trusted Foundry accreditation. NSA->defense microelectronics lineage. Trusted Foundry Access III ~$576M ceiling (DMEA 2026).
